o1.biggest_strength: A concrete plan with dates: a data check on Team 8+ single-user accounts, then a dated test, then a dated launch, backed by low, mid and high scenarios that use our real numbers.
o1.biggest_mistake: It drops the yearly-billing push as a 'runner-up', even though yearly payers churn 0.9% vs 4.0% a month and we never offer yearly after signup. Its test only covers new visitors, so it never measures churn among the existing 8+ customers who are actually leaving.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add an honest in-app yearly offer, and test Agency on the existing at-risk Essentials 8+ base with a churn-based stop rule.

o2.biggest_strength: It goes straight at the 9.6% churn leak with correct revenue math, tests on existing Essentials 8+ customers against a control group and on a slice of Team 8+ to measure downgrades, and sets clear go and stop thresholds.
o2.biggest_mistake: Yearly billing only appears as an offer at the moment of switching. It is not a broader fix to the monthly default or the missing post-signup yearly offer, which could be the fastest win inside two quarters.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a separate, cheap yearly-default and in-app yearly offer test with its own math, and give launch dates mapped to the board's two-quarter window.

reason: Both pick the right fix and get the numbers right. Output 2 tests it on the customers who are actually leaving, sets churn-based stop rules, uses our 'here's exactly what you'd pay' voice, and at least brings in yearly billing, which Output 1 dismissed.
